verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews who lived in the land of Egypt, who lived at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Memphis, and in the country of Pathros, saying,

“Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘You have seen all the evil that I have brought on Jerusalem, and on all the cities of Judah. Behold, today they are a desolation, and no man dwells therein,
because of their wickedness which they have committed to provoke me to anger, in that they went to burn incense, to serve other gods, that they didn’t know, neither they, nor you, nor your fathers.
However I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them, saying, “Oh, don’t do this abominable thing that I hate.”
But they didn’t listen and didn’t incline their ear. They didn’t turn from their wickedness, to stop burning incense to other gods.
Therefore my wrath and my anger was poured out, and was kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they are wasted and desolate, as it is today.’

“Therefore now Yahweh, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Why do you commit great evil against your own souls, to cut off from yourselves man and woman, infant and nursing child out of the middle of Judah, to leave yourselves no one remaining;

in that you provoke me to anger with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have gone to live; that you may be cut off, and that you may be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

Have you forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, and the wickedness of the kings of Judah, and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives which they committed in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?
They are not humbled even to this day, neither have they feared, nor walked in my law, nor in my statutes, that I set before you and before your fathers.’
“Therefore Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will set my face against you for evil, even to cut off all Judah.

I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt to live there, and they will all be consumed. They will fall in the land of Egypt. They will be consumed by the sword and by the famine. They will die, from the least even to the greatest, by the sword and by the famine. They will be an object of horror, an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach.
For I will punish those who dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence;

so that none of the remnant of Judah, who have gone into the land of Egypt to live there, shall escape or be left, to return into the land of Judah, to which they have a desire to return to dwell there; for no one will return except those who will escape.’”

Then all the men who knew that their wives burned incense to other gods, and all the women who stood by, a great assembly, even all the people who lived in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
“As for the word that you have spoken to us in Yahweh’s name, we will not listen to you.

But we will certainly perform every word that has gone out of our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we have done, we and our fathers, our kings and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem; for then had we plenty of food, and were well, and saw no evil.
But since we stopped burning incense to the queen of the sky, and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.
“When we burned incense to the queen of the sky, and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings to her, without our husbands?”
Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men, and to the women, even to all the people who had given him an answer, saying,

“The incense that you burned in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, you and your fathers, your kings and your princes, and the people of the land, didn’t Yahweh remember them, and didn’t it come into his mind?

Thus Yahweh could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings, and because of the abominations which you have committed; therefore your land has become a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is today.

Because you have burned incense, and because you have sinned against Yahweh, and have not obeyed Yahweh’s voice, nor walked in his law, nor in his statutes, nor in his testimonies; therefore this evil has happened to you, as it is today.”
Moreover Jeremiah said to all the people, and to all the women, “Hear Yahweh’s word, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt!

Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says, ‘You and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and with your hands have fulfilled it, saying, “We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to her.” “‘Establish then your vows, and perform your vows.’

“Therefore hear Yahweh’s word, all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt: ‘Behold, I have sworn by my great name,’ says Yahweh, ‘that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, “As the Lord Yahweh lives.”
Behold, I watch over them for evil, and not for good; and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until they are all gone.

Those who escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, few in number; and all the remnant of Judah, who have gone into the land of Egypt to live there, shall know whose word shall stand, mine, or theirs.
“‘This shall be the sign to you,’ says Yahweh, ‘that I will punish you in this place, that you may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil.’

Yahweh says, ‘Behold, I will give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of those who seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who was his enemy, and sought his life.’”

footnotes.content: Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis—cities where God's people scattered after Jerusalem fell, hoping to find safety. But even in exile, they carried their old unfaithfulness with them. Distance from home doesn't distance us from the Lord's gaze.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah speaks hard truth first: I have brought this destruction. God doesn't hide behind circumstances—He claims His judgment openly. There's a strange mercy in that honesty, because it means judgment comes from a Father who grieves what He must do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They burned incense to gods 'that they didn't know'—a penetrating phrase. Not ignorant by accident, but by choice; they turned from the God who was near to worship what was foreign and false. How often do we settle for shadows when we have known the Light?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God sent prophets 'rising up early'—an image of His persistent, urgent love. He keeps showing up with His call before dawn, before people's minds close for the day. And still they didn't listen. How patient the Lord is, and how stubborn we can be.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three times they refused: didn't listen, didn't incline their ear, didn't turn. Refusal becomes a pattern, a hardening. We become what we practice—and they practiced turning away. The saddest servitude is the one we choose ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wrath poured out, anger kindled—the Lord's judgment is not cold detachment but burning response to what He loves spoiled by idolatry. The desolation was already visible then, and still is. Some ruins teach harder lessons than stones can speak.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why do you commit evil against your own souls? The question cuts to the absurdity: their rebellion was really self-harm dressed as defiance. We do the same—call it freedom when it's self-erasure. The Lord asks not in anger but in bewilderment at our choice to wound ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even in Egypt, they burned incense to idols—as if distance made the old sin a new one. They thought leaving Jerusalem meant leaving God's judgment, but Judah's God is not confined to Judah. Exile doesn't hide us from the eyes that see all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chain of wickedness—fathers, kings, wives, wives of wives—goes back generations. We inherit not just history but the ruts our forebears wore. Yet each of us stands in the present before the Lord. Our parents' sins are theirs; ours are ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not humbled, not afraid, not walking in His law—each refusal deeper than the last. They had seen the city burn, yet their hearts remained hard as the ash. Sometimes we learn everything except repentance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will set my face against you—the words are dreadful not because God is capricious, but because His face is the very thing we need most. To have Him against us is exile itself, no matter what land we call home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The remnant—those who escaped the sword in Jerusalem—imagined safety in Egypt. But judgment followed them like a shadow they could not outrun. From least to greatest, none escape. The Lord's word, once spoken, is a pursuing mercy we cannot flee.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The plagues of Egypt—sword, famine, pestilence—visit the exiles as they visited the nation long before. History circles back. We forget the lessons God teaches through others' ruin and find ourselves standing in the same ruins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: None shall escape except those who escape—a paradox that holds the truth. Even judgment carries a whisper of grace for the few who turn. Hope lingers at the edge of threat, waiting for anyone willing to hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the people gathered in assembly in Egypt—the entire community united not in faith but in defiance. There's a power in corporate rebellion, but it's the power of a ship with all hands on the rudder steering toward the rocks. Pathros was deep Egypt; they were as far from home as exile could make them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We will not listen to you—a direct refusal, spoken aloud where everyone can hear. Sometimes people need to say their 'no' in public so they cannot later pretend they did not choose it. Our refusals often reveal us to ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We will certainly perform every word—they swear loyalty to their vow to burn incense to the 'queen of the sky,' and they remember when 'we had plenty of food, were well, and saw no evil.' But memory is a liar; they remember good years and forget whose hand provided them. Gratitude to false gods is blindness to the true Giver.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Since we stopped burning incense, we've had nothing—they read poverty as the price of abandoning their idols. They mistook correlation for causation, mistook the consequence of exile for the cost of righteousness. Suffering blinds us to truth unless we let the Lord open our eyes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Did we make her cakes without our husbands' permission? They ask as if the women were powerless, yet they invoke this memory with pride—a strange reversal where they claim innocence through necessity. We are skilled at remaking our disobedience as circumstance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah speaks to all—men and women, everyone who answered him. He will not let the people hide behind roles or excuses. The word of truth goes out to every ear without exception, because every soul answers to God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Didn't Yahweh remember them, didn't it come into His mind? The question assumes they think God forgets or ignores. But the Almighty's memory is perfect and terrible; nothing hidden escapes His knowing. Our deepest fear should be not that He sees, but that He sees and we refuse to be seen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh could no longer bear—even the patient God reaches a limit when love is spurned and abomination embraced. But this is not petulance; it is the moment when mercy must yield to truth. A land without God becomes a desolation, a prophecy in stones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Because—the whole chain collapses into one word. They burned incense, sinned, didn't listen, didn't obey, didn't walk in His law. Each step was a choice; each choice had weight. There is no accident in judgment; it is the harvest of seeds we planted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah calls to all—men and women both—to hear the Lord's word. No one is exempt from this summons. Even now, even after defiance, the prophet speaks, giving them one more chance to turn their ears toward home and toward God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You have spoken with your mouths, and with your hands fulfilled it—they made vows to the queen of heaven and kept them with fierce devotion. Here God does something strange: He doesn't forbid them; He tells them to finish what they swore. Sometimes the sharpest judgment is letting us have what we insisted we wanted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I have sworn by my great name—Yahweh's oath stands against theirs. They vowed to burn incense; He vows His name will vanish from their mouths. When God's word and human will collide, God's word stands. Yet how we resist this truth until we see it carved into history.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I watch over them for evil, not for good—a terrible reversal of the promise to watch over and protect. When we turn from God, His care becomes a terrible thing. Even His watching becomes part of our judgment because we are watched by One whose love we have rejected.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo here: a few escape the sword to return, and through them God's word stands proven. We see again how often His judgment leaves room for a remnant, a seed from which something can grow again. As of 2026-10, I am grateful the Lord is never wholly finished with His people, even when correction must come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This shall be the sign—God Himself guarantees what Jeremiah speaks. The sign is history itself; when it comes to pass, they will know whose word stands. We too see signs around us every day; the question is whether we have eyes to see that the Lord keeps His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pharaoh Hophra given to his enemies, as Zedekiah was given to Nebuchadnezzar—the Lord's hand is at work even in Egypt's throne room and Babylon's court. The kings of earth who think themselves beyond reach are themselves in the hand of the God who sees all nations and judges all rulers. No crown escapes His gaze.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
